tool.title: Candidate translations — agent model
tool.description: An agent model proposes a translation for each string of a layer's catalogues, with the locale term base and the string's source context in front of it, and appends them to each catalogue's candidates sidecar with `source.kind: agent` and the model's id. Seeds an empty `msgstr` with the first candidate, fuzzy.

inputs.name: instance
inputs.description: The layer root whose catalogues to propose for. Default: the current layer.

inputs.name: locales
inputs.description: The target locales. Absent: every locale the layer declares.

outputs.name: candidates
outputs.description: `translations/<locale>/<catalogue>.candidates.json` (`translation-candidates/v1`), appended to; each candidate carries `source: {kind: "agent", id: <model>}`.

outputs.name: catalogues
outputs.description: The `.po` catalogues whose empty `msgstr` got the first candidate, `#, fuzzy`.

selection.when: Prose that needs the surrounding meaning — paragraphs, diagram labels whose sense depends on the process, terms the locale term base fixes — and an agent session is already running.
selection.limits: Not reproducible run to run, and its output is as unreviewed as any engine's. For many short, literal strings an open machine-translation model (OPUS-MT, LibreTranslate / Argos, through `translation:candidates`) is cheaper and repeatable.
selection.cost: Model tokens per string, in a session that has a model; nothing to install.

$comment.comment: The agent is the session already running; it reaches no host this Tool adds.

`manual`: the agent is the session, following `translation-candidate-source`; there is no command. The open machine-translation engines are ONE Tool, `translation-candidates` (`bun run cat translation:candidates --engine opus-mt,libretranslate`, cat-harness#1329), which picks its engine by flag rather than being a node per engine.
